freshness_check: Both reviewed angles concern the September 11th pollock paper, not KGS.

angle_b.assessment: Strongest affirmative thesis: learning can discover alternatives worth testing. Its scenario distinctions largely match F09 to F13.
angle_b.challenge: The falsifier overreaches. Conventional rules matching learned rules wouldn't erase the demonstrated capacity to discover choices, though it would weaken a claim of superior research value. The ending about acceptable annual swings also narrows away the Ricker biomass tradeoff.

angle_c.assessment: The second movement correctly requires a separate experiment and a separate baseline. It fairly rejects equating lower biomass with unsafe depletion.
angle_c.challenge: The title A Smoother Catch Has a Cost and wording catch pattern smooths may conflate the shape of the Ricker harvest-policy response with demonstrated annual catch stability. F12 verifies a smoother learned policy. It doesn't establish lower annual catch variance than the conventional comparison. Don't frame lower breeding biomass as the causal price of smoothing catches.

strongest_revision: Use B's affirmative policy-discovery thesis, followed by A's biological-assumption reversal. Constant recruitment: large annual catch swings alongside higher spawning biomass. Ricker recruitment: a smoother policy response and higher catches alongside lower spawning biomass. All comparisons remain scoped to the simulated cases.
revised_falsifier: A corrected or reproduced analysis that removes the reported scenario-specific differences would defeat this account. Failure to outperform an equally developed conventional rule would defeat superiority, which isn't the proposed thesis.
earned_second_movement: Changing recruitment reverses the direction of the breeding-stock comparison. That is substantive without claiming the second case solves annual stability.
ending_focus: Which combination of catches, annual stability and breeding biomass should candidate rules have to demonstrate in further testing?
